sentences.text: The name Camuropiscis translates to "flat-nosed fish," reflecting its most distinctive feature.
This species possessed a flattened, elongated snout that likely improved its hydrodynamic streamlining for efficient swimming.
Only four recorded fossil occurrences of this ancient creature are known to science.
All discovered remains come from the Gogo Formation in Kimberley, Western Australia.
The genus Camuropiscis was formally described by Dennis and Miles in 1979.
Taxonomically, Camuropiscis is classified within the class Placodermi, a group of armored fish.
It belongs to the family Camuropiscidae.
Further classification places it in the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, the clade Coccosteomorphi, and the larger group Eubrachythoraci.
The type species of the genus is Camuropiscis concinnus, which serves as the reference specimen for the group.
Fossils of Camuropiscis date to the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
This animal lived between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
